title: Seasonal influenza including influenza A (H1N1): categorisation and oseltamivir (India)
specialty: Infectious Diseases / Internal Medicine / Paediatrics / Public Health

evidenceAudit.scope: Seasonal influenza, including influenza A (H1N1), in adults, children, infants and pregnancy in India: high-risk groups, Category A/B/C triage, oseltamivir treatment and prophylaxis, severe disease and infection control, built on the MoHFW Clinical Management Protocol for Seasonal Influenza (revised February 2019).
findings: Category A and B not needing admission, Category C immediate admission and laboratory confirmation, oseltamivir for all Category B and C started within 48 hours without waiting for tests, oseltamivir doses by weight and age including infants and preterm infants, 5-day course with extension in severe or immunocompromised patients, staff prophylaxis 75 mg daily for 7 days, high-risk groups, pregnancy advice, intensive care unit (ICU) and ventilation thresholds, antibiotics for secondary pneumonia, isolation and PPE checked against the MoHFW protocol (2019).
unverifiedSections: The opened protocol text did not include the full clinical definitions of Category A, B(i), B(ii) and C; the triage below uses the actions stated (no admission for A and B, admission for C, oseltamivir for B and C). Clinician to confirm against the full MoHFW categorisation chart.
Renal dose adjustment of oseltamivir was not in the opened protocol.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Influenza is an acute viral respiratory infection with seasonal peaks in India, often during the monsoon and winter. Influenza A (H1N1) and other strains cause fever, cough and sore throat; most people recover, but pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and death occur, especially in high-risk groups: age 65 or more, pregnancy and up to 2 weeks postpartum, children under 5, chronic heart, lung, kidney, liver or neurological disease, diabetes, immunosuppression and severe obesity (MoHFW 2019). India uses a Category A/B/C triage: A and B are managed at home, C is admitted; Category B and C patients receive oseltamivir within 48 hours without waiting for test results.
keyMechanisms: Influenza virus infects respiratory epithelium via haemagglutinin binding.
Viral replication and the host inflammatory response cause fever and airway damage.
Severe infection causes viral pneumonia and ARDS.
Damaged epithelium allows secondary bacterial pneumonia.

symptoms: Fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose
Breathlessness or chest pain in severe disease
redFlags: Breathlessness, chest pain, falling SpO2: Category C, admit (MoHFW 2019)
SpO2 below 90% or PaO2 below 60 mmHg on FiO2 below 0.6 despite oxygen: ventilation (MoHFW 2019)
Haemodynamic instability or multi-organ dysfunction: ICU (MoHFW 2019)
Deterioration after initial improvement: suspect bacterial pneumonia (MoHFW 2019)
precipitants: Close contact with an infected person

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Test for SARS-CoV-2; loss of smell.
High fever, myalgia, low platelets, no prominent cough.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: No hospitalisation needed; Category B patients receive oseltamivir.
Admit immediately; confirm by real-time RT-PCR; give oseltamivir.

Age 65 or more; pregnancy and 2 weeks postpartum; children under 5 (especially under 2); chronic heart, lung, kidney, liver or neurological disease; diabetes; haemoglobinopathies; immunosuppression; BMI 40 or more.

clinicalManagement.title: Categorise
actions: Ask about high-risk conditions and danger signs (MoHFW 2019).
Category A and B: home care and isolation; Category C: admit immediately (MoHFW 2019).

clinicalManagement.title: Oseltamivir
actions: All Category B and C: oseltamivir, ideally within 48 hours; do not wait for test results (MoHFW 2019).
Usual course 5 days; extend if immunocompromised or severe lower respiratory disease (MoHFW 2019).

clinicalManagement.title: Severe disease
actions: Oxygen; ICU for respiratory failure, haemodynamic instability or multi-organ dysfunction (MoHFW 2019).
Mild ARDS may trial early NIV; moderate to severe needs invasive ventilation (MoHFW 2019).
Add antibiotics as for community-acquired pneumonia for severe presentation, deterioration after improvement or no improvement after 3–5 days (MoHFW 2019).

clinicalManagement.title: Infection control
actions: Isolation room or cohort ward with beds at least 1 m apart; PPE for staff (MoHFW 2019).
Home isolation for 7 days from symptom onset (MoHFW 2019).

clinicalManagement.title: Pregnancy
actions: Start oseltamivir within 48 hours without waiting for results (MoHFW 2019).
Vaccinate at any gestation; breastfeeding encouraged (MoHFW 2019).

medicationPlan.note: All doses are from the MoHFW Clinical Management Protocol for Seasonal Influenza (2019). India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

learningObjectives: Triage into categories A, B and C.
Dose oseltamivir by age and weight.
keyPoints: Category B and C: oseltamivir within 48 hours, no waiting for tests.
Adults 75 mg twice daily for 5 days.
Category C: admit and confirm by RT-PCR.
Pregnancy is high risk: treat early.
pitfalls: No antibiotics when bacterial pneumonia follows.

patientEducation: Stay home for 7 days from symptom onset (MoHFW 2019).
Cover coughs and sneezes; wash hands.
Return for breathlessness, chest pain or drowsiness.
lifestyleAndDiet: Annual influenza vaccination for high-risk groups and pregnancy.
